$comment: Economic nexus thresholds and SaaS taxability, per state.
READ THIS BEFORE RELYING ON ANY ROW BELOW.
This file is a working data set maintained by hand. It is NOT tax advice and
it is NOT authoritative. Every row carries a `status`:
verified   — checked against a cited source on `verified_on`.
unverified — structure only. scripts/nexus-report.mjs refuses to score
these and lists them separately, so an empty row can never
be silently read as 'no exposure'.
Two things make this data go stale fast, and both have moved recently:
transaction-count tests are being repealed one state at a time (Alaska 2025,
Utah 2025, Illinois 2026, North Carolina), and SaaS taxability is decided
state by state with no federal standard.
For a business actually approaching a threshold, the right answer is a
service that tracks this for you — Stripe Tax is already one integration away
given checkout runs on Stripe, and Avalara and TaxJar do the same job. Hand
maintenance of 46 taxing jurisdictions is not a good use of a solo founder's
week, and being wrong is expensive in a way that being late is not.
WHY THE TRANSACTION TEST MATTERS MORE THAN THE DOLLAR TEST HERE:
at $149/month a customer bills 12 times a year and produces $1,788. The
$100,000 test therefore needs roughly 56 customers in one state. A 200
transaction test needs roughly 17. In the states that still have one, the
count is reached about three times sooner than the revenue — which is the
opposite of most people's intuition and the reason this file exists.
Whether each monthly invoice counts as its own transaction is not uniformly
settled and is flagged per state as `recurring_counts_per_invoice`. Where it
is null, nobody here has confirmed it. Ask a professional before treating a
null as a no.

general_rules.$comment: Verified. Use these to sanity-check any individual row.
notes: TX taxes 80% of a SaaS charge, treating it as a data processing service.
AK has no statewide tax but local jurisdictions levy one through the ARSSTC.
CO and IL contain home-rule localities that set their own rules.
IA and OH distinguish business from consumer purchasers.
NY's test is conjunctive: $500,000 AND 100 transactions, both required.

states.$comment: Seeded from the verified general rules above. A state is only marked verified where the specific combination below was confirmed, not merely inferred from the aggregate counts.

CA.note: B2B SaaS generally exempt with no download or tangible media.

NY.note: Conjunctive — both tests must be met.

TX.note: 80% of the charge is taxable as data processing.

AK.note: No statewide tax; local ARSSTC jurisdictions. 200-transaction test repealed 2025-01-01.

IL.note: Transaction test repealed 2026-01-01. Home-rule localities differ.

HI.note: General excise tax rather than a sales tax.

CT.note: Believed conjunctive and at a distinct rate for SaaS. Confirm both.

CO.note: Home-rule localities set their own rules.

NE.note: SaaS generally untaxed, but security-function software is a taxable service.
